vocabulary.definition: A state of matter in which atoms are stripped of their electrons, resulting in a hot, electrically charged gas.
vocabulary.example: The plasma in the Sun is so hot that the nuclei and electrons can separate and flow around freely.

vocabulary.definition: A substance that dissolves a solute, resulting in a solution.
vocabulary.example: If we brought a solvent of the chromosphere to Earth, it would immediately be crushed by the atmospheric pressure.

vocabulary.definition: Small, bright regions on the surface of the Sun that are the tops of convection cells.
vocabulary.example: The photosphere of the Sun is covered in a grid of a million hot spots called granules.

vocabulary.definition: Relating to or using nuclear reactions that occur only at very high temperatures.
vocabulary.example: Bringing matter from the radiative zone of the Sun to our lab would result in an explosion with the power of a thermonuclear weapon.

vocabulary.definition: A small, dense, and extremely hot star that is typically the size of a planet.
vocabulary.example: In billions of years, the core of the Sun will remain as a white dwarf after its death.

vocabulary.definition: Relating to or involving widespread devastation or ultimate disaster.
vocabulary.example: If the Sun's core were brought to Earth, the resulting explosion would be apocalyptic, possibly ending human civilization.
